transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I just haven’t been doing anything. I mostly sit in my room, wearing the same clothes. I used to knit and write in my journal and go for walks, but I don’t really do that anymore. When my mom asks what’s wrong, I can barely answer her.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time?
I don’t know. I wouldn’t say sad exactly… mostly just kind of blank, I guess.
Do you still enjoy the things you used to like doing, like knitting and writing in your journal?
Not really. I just… don’t pick them up anymore. My knitting, my journal… I used to go walking too, but now I mostly just sit in my room. I can’t really make myself do it.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure in things that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. It’s not like I hate those things, I just don’t really feel anything about them anymore. I don’t knit or write or go walking. Mostly I just sit in my room, and even answering my mom feels like too much.
How long have you been feeling this way?
I think… since I started that community college program. So, a little over two years ago… maybe two years and a couple months.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since you started feeling this way?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed. My clothes seem about the same, I guess.
Do you feel like you're moving slower or faster than you used to?
I’m… not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed moving faster or anything. Maybe I’m just slower getting around sometimes, but I don’t know.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself?
I… I don’t really want to talk about that. I’m not sure.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about anything?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I just don’t really think about it that clearly.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to, most of the time?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it most of the time.
Have you been having thoughts about hurting yourself that you feel comfortable sharing with me?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really feel comfortable talking about that.
Have you been having any thoughts about ending your life?
I… I’m not sure. I don’t really want to talk about that right now.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been checking my weight or anything… I don’t think I noticed a big change.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless a lot?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I haven’t really been paying attention to that.
Have you been having any thoughts about ending your life that you feel you can share with me now?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really want to get into it.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety most of the time?
I don’t really know… I mean, sometimes maybe, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it most of the time.
Have you been having any thoughts about ending your life that you feel you can share with me now?
I… I’m not really sure how to talk about that. I don’t think I can say much right now.
Are you having thoughts about ending your life?
I… I don’t know. I’m not sure I can answer that right now.
Are you currently having thoughts about ending your life?
I… I’m not sure. I don’t really want to get into it right now.
Are you having thoughts of ending your life right now?
I… I can’t really say. I don’t know how to answer that right now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of feeling blank, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, and significant decrease in productivity, which have been present for over two years, meet the criteria for a Major Depressive Disorder. The lack of clear expression of sadness and the predominant feeling of emptiness, along with the absence of sufficient information to confirm psychotic symptoms or melancholic features, lead towards the diagnosis of a single episode of Major Depressive Disorder without specification of severity or presence of psychotic or melancholic features.
